acceptance_criteria: All 4 tests pass. Walking direction confirmed correct by checking which SPKI verifies which cert.
description:
Implement the reverse-walk loop skeleton and the two per-cert checks that
require crypto (signature) and name comparison (issuer linkage).

## What

After find_trust_anchor() returns anchor_index, initialize:
  working_issuer_name = anchor.subject
  working_spki        = anchor.subject_public_key_info

Walk i in (0..chain.len()).rev():
  a. verifier.verify_signature(algorithm, working_spki, tbs_bytes, sig_bytes)
     -> Err(Error::SignatureInvalid { index: i }) on failure
  b. names_match(working_issuer_name, cert[i].tbs.issuer)
     -> Err(Error::ChainBroken { index: i }) on mismatch

  End of iteration state update:
     working_spki        = cert[i].tbs.subject_public_key_info
     working_issuer_name = cert[i].tbs.subject

## Notes
- The loop at this stage does NOT yet include validity/extension/CA checks (those are PKIX-h6z-val).
- tbs_bytes are the DER-encoded TBSCertificate — extract from the raw cert bytes, not re-encode.
- Walk direction: reverse (issuer-to-leaf) is correct per RFC 5280 §6.1.3.

## Tests (externally-generated DER hex literals, openssl verify as oracle)
- 1-cert chain: verify_signature called once with anchor SPKI, names_match called once
- 3-cert chain: verify_signature called 3x, state correctly threaded leaf→int→root
- Leaf with bad signature (flip one byte) -> SignatureInvalid { index: 0 }
- Intermediate with wrong issuer name -> ChainBroken { index: 1 }

## Depends on
PKIX-yqb (find_trust_anchor), PKIX-q13 (SignatureVerifier returns own error, not chain-indexed), PKIX-drv (names_match)
title: pkix-path: chain walk loop — signature verification and name linkage
